claim: Chiang Wan-an of the Kuomintang is re-elected mayor of Taipei in Taiwan's local elections on Saturday 28 November 2026.

runs.scenario: If voting takes place within the window but the CEC count does not establish Chiang as the top vote-getter until after 23:59, one reader could resolve YES because the window applies to when the election is held, while another could resolve NO because the winning result was not established within the window.
runs.yes_requires: The Taipei City mayoral election must be held within the stated 08:00–23:59 window on 28 November 2026 (Asia/Taipei), and the Central Election Commission's count must show Chiang Wan-an receiving more votes than any other candidate.
runs.decided_by: Taiwan's Central Election Commission results site. If that site cannot be read, Focus Taiwan/CNA reporting of the CEC count decides. Later recounts or court challenges do not change the resolution.

runs.yes_requires: The Taipei City mayoral election must be held on 28 November 2026 (Asia/Taipei), and the Central Election Commission's initial count must show Chiang Wan-an with the most votes.
runs.decided_by: Taiwan's Central Election Commission (via db.cec.gov.tw or its 2026 results site), or Focus Taiwan/CNA reporting of the CEC count if the CEC site cannot be read.

runs.scenario: Some Taipei districts vote on 28 Nov 2026 and others are postponed to a later date; the eventual CEC total shows Chiang Wan-an first. One reader treats the election as not held on 28 Nov, or excludes votes outside the window, and resolves NO; the other treats it as held that day and uses the combined CEC count, resolving YES.
